# dsh-video-vision
English | 简体中文
> Gives DeepSeek Harness eyes for video.

Harness models already read images. They cannot open a video: no tool turns a clip into
something a

text-and-image model can look at. **dsh-video-vision** adds the missing step —
one tool, `read_video

`, that decodes a video, samples frames across it, and hands those
frames back as images the model c

decodes a video, samples frames across it, and hands those
frames back as images the model can see.
Ask in plain language:
> 帮我看看这段视频讲了什么
> What happens at the 12 second mark?
> Read the slides in this screen recording. Can you summarize them?
> Does this clip show anyone picking up a red object?
## Before and after
| | Without this plugin | With this plugin |
| A video file | "I can only read text and images." | The model describes the scenes and answers que

stions about them |
| On-screen text | You retype the slides | The model reads the frames itself |
|

"What happens at 0:12?" | Not possible | One call with `timestamps: [12]` |
| Spoken words | Not he
ard | Subtitle track or sidecar file, quoted with timestamps; audio transcription when a speech-to-t

ext provider is mounted |
| When was it filmed | Unknown | Container metadata: recording date, devic

is mounted |
| When was it filmed | Unknown | Container metadata: recording date, device, location |

What it does **not** do: watch every frame in real time. It looks at N sampled stills
(8 by default)

, placed where the picture changes most, with the rest spaced evenly. A
moment shorter than the samp

ling interval can still be missed — pass `timestamps` when you
know where to look.

The tool appears as `read_video`. Nothing else changes: models without a video request
keep working

s `read_video`. Nothing else changes: models without a video request
keep working exactly as before.
### Requirements

1. **An image-capable model.** The current route must declare image input (DeepSeek V41
Flash does).

On a text-only model the tool refuses with a message naming the model,
instead of uploading frames

the provider would reject.
2. **An ffmpeg executable.** Resolved in this order, first working candid

der would reject.
2. **An ffmpeg executable.** Resolved in this order, first working candidate wins:
| # | Source | Notes |

| 1 | `ffmpegPath` plugin config | explicit path, no guessing |
| 2 | decoder bundled by this packag

e | `@ffmpeg-installer/ffmpeg` is an optional dependency; no install script runs |
| 3 | `DSH_FFMPEG

` environment variable | for people who keep ffmpeg in an unusual place |
| 4 | system `PATH` | `win

get install Gyan.FFmpeg`, `brew install ffmpeg`, `apt install ffmpeg` |
| 5 | usual install location

s | WinGet links, Chocolatey, Scoop, `/usr/local/bin`, Homebrew, … |
| 6 | time-boxed directory scan
| user app directories, result cached under `$DSH_HOME/cache/dsh-video-vision` |
If none is found, the tool fails with the exact commands above rather than a stack trace.
## The `read_video` tool
| Parameter | Type | Meaning |
| `path` | string, **required** | Video file path, resolved by the filesystem backend (a relative pa

th uses the session workspace) |
| `frames` | number | How many frames to sample, capped by config |
| `timestamps` | number[] | Explicit positions in seconds; overrides `frames`, sorted, clamped into

the clip |
| `start` / `end` | number | Sampling window in seconds; defaults to the whole clip |
|

`width` | number | Long edge of one frame in pixels; never upscales |
| `transcript` | boolean | Ask

the mounted speech-to-text provider for a transcript |
| `subtitles` | boolean | Include subtitle t

ext the file already carries |
| `layout` | `auto` \| `frames` \| `grid` | Contact sheet once the co

unt reaches the config threshold, or one image per moment |
| `carry` | string | Summary of an earli

er chunk; this read continues from it instead of starting over |
| `text` | boolean | Read on-screen

text as the primary content (news, talking head, tutorial, screen recording) |
| `language` | strin
g | Language hint for the transcript, and for choosing among subtitle tracks |

Moments follow the content, not the clock: slots go to shots that actually change, a still
shot is c

apped at one frame, and two samples showing the same picture are collapsed into one
(`sampling.dedup

ed` says how many). Text-first reads the other way — an even sweep that keeps
every moment, because
burned-in subtitles change while the picture does not.
What the model receives (contact-sheet layout):
[代码示例省略，未执行]

The delta table counts the cuts that sit between two moments, using the same proxy the shot
detector

uses. Counting beats measuring the peak change: past a few seconds every gap contains
a cut, so a p

eak-based table says "large" everywhere and tells the model nothing. Cut density
stays comparable ac

ross a 25-second edit and a 4-minute vlog — one cut in three seconds is fast
cutting in both. The pr

otocol asks for difference → prediction → check, because one pass of
"summarise this video" misses c
uts and invents continuity.
### Reading a long video in chunks

`read_video` returns one window at a time. To keep the later part coherent, hand the earlier
summary

rns one window at a time. To keep the later part coherent, hand the earlier
summary back as `carry`:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

Each call then starts by checking the carried claims against what the new moments show, so
mistakes
from the beginning are fixed later instead of being repeated.
## Configuration

Every field is optional; the shipped values are the defaults. Set them on the
`video-vision` row of
the plugin's config.

This build declares no config schema, so the plugin panel shows no settings form. To
